context: Batch review B1 (PX-3585): TerminalCapabilities::allows was wired into four production checks but the only production constructor inserted a single wildcard entry, so allows(t, scope) equalled granted.contains(scope) for every terminal and TerminalCapabilities::grant had no production caller. The reviewer offered two options: wire a real per-terminal grant source, or narrow the issue and evidence to say per-terminal narrowing is deferred. The commander chose the real grant source.
decision_body: A consent-issued automation bearer is the production per-terminal grant. issue_automation_bearer_for_connection records the family terminal scope (Synthesize to terminal.input, Capture and FrameDigest to terminal.inspect) in the issuing session via ControlAuthority::grant_terminal_capability, which clamps the grant to the connection own scopes so a binding can never widen. Semantics: a terminal with an entry is answered by that entry alone (intersection), grants are additive per terminal so family order never traps a client, and an emptied entry is removed so the terminal falls back to the connection wildcard. Revoke, session-end revoke, and expiry release only the capability no other live bearer of the same session still binds. Every failure mode of the mechanism is over-narrow (deny), never over-broad (allow). The ctl control verbs and the debug read surfaces now observe a real narrowing: a read-only binding on t:1 may read t:1, may not drive it, and leaves other terminals untouched. The debug read contract is a coarse debug scope intersected with terminal.inspect (P1-3 resolved by documenting the narrowing rule rather than dropping it).

consequences: Opt-in via JobRegistry::with_job_cgroups; JobRegistry::new keeps Missing(NotConfigured). A fork-before-placement descendant OOM kill is invisible (documented). Race-free placement would need an unsafe-reviewed spawn boundary (clone3 CLONE_INTO_CGROUP), which is out of scope.
context: Issue 1537 needs OomKilled evidence from per-job cgroup memory.events on Linux. bitty-pty forbids unsafe code, so pre_exec and clone3 CLONE_INTO_CGROUP are unavailable; no new FFI crates allowed.
decision_body: Discovery: JobCgroups::discover reads the 0:: line of /proc/self/cgroup (rejecting non-normal components) and the cgroup2 mount point with root / from /proc/self/mountinfo, then tries the own cgroup and its parent as the hosting parent; the host must list memory in cgroup.subtree_control and allow mkdir. A dedicated empty base bitty-jobs-PID-SEQ with +memory hosts leaves job-ID-GENERATION (no-internal-processes rule). JobCgroups::under injects the parent. Placement: the supervisor creates the leaf and reads oom_kill before spawn, then writes the leader pid into cgroup.procs immediately after spawn, before tree adoption and drains. Residual window: descendants forked between exec and that write stay outside the leaf and are not accounted. Cleanup: after reap and tree kill, write cgroup.kill then rmdir with bounded retries; unremovable leaves stay on a bounded list, count against MAX_JOB_CGROUP_LEAVES, and are retried; the base is removed on drop. Evidence: every JobSnapshot carries OomEvidence, with a typed OomEvidenceGap when missing; only an advanced counter plus SIGKILL yields OomKilled.
title: CTX-0880: per-job cgroup v2 leaf placement and delegated-subtree discovery

consequences: On a systemd desktop discover() returns NotDelegated unless bitty runs inside a Delegate=yes unit that has moved its processes into a child cgroup; otherwise the host must configure JobCgroups::under. Live tests need BITTY_TEST_DELEGATED_CGROUP or a delegated namespace root, and skip otherwise.
context: Review PX-4170 found that DEC-0081 discovery adopted the parent cgroup (a systemd-managed app.slice without user.delegate) because mkdir succeeded, which moved job leaders out of the owner scope. It also found that a host-delivered SIGKILL on an OOM-evidenced job was classified OomKilled.
decision_body: Discovery uses only the process own cgroup and only when it is the cgroup-namespace root (0:: path /) or carries the user.delegate or trusted.delegate xattr with value 1, read via rustix::fs::getxattr (safe API; rustix 1.1 fs feature already enabled for bitty-runtime; no new crate or feature). There is no ancestor fallback. The qualifying cgroup must already enable memory in cgroup.subtree_control; the delegator moves its own processes into a child first, and bitty never moves processes it did not spawn. JobCgroups::under is the explicit-configuration path with no marker check. Base creation sweeps stale siblings that are exactly named bitty-jobs-PID-SEQ, whose PID is dead and whose cgroup.events shows populated 0, one rmdir each, bounded by MAX_STALE_BASE_SWEEP. The leaf bound equals the registry capacity. A SIGKILL sent by the host (signal_as Kill, killing cancel, or deadline) classifies as Signaled(9); an advanced counter stays only as OomEvidence::OomKilled. Supersedes the discovery and classification parts of DEC-0081; its placement-window design stands.
title: CTX-0880: per-job cgroup discovery requires explicit delegation; host kills are never OomKilled

decision_body: Owner correction superseding the add-API reading of the program. Bitty has an upstream Rust layer and a downstream Lua layer. decision_body: Owner: the end-state crate count (~14-15) is acceptable; the requirement is that everything not belonging to the terminal leaves Core, and that the resulting architecture is well-organized and maintainable. Each extraction is: create the crate in the extension repo with its contract, move code, wire the dependency, delete from Core, prove parity with the moved tests. decision_body:
# CTX-1142 styling-system design brief (design output only, no code)

Owner direction (binding): Lua-first code-as-config growing on the appearance
tree; NO taffy — the cell-grid solver stays the sole layout authority; a
text-stylesheet grammar comes only later as a `bitty-style` extension.
This brief is the complete design record; implementation is explicitly out of
scope for this task.

Conventions used below: `appearance.*` = the Lua `appearance = {...}` table
and its typed owners (`appearance.theme/colors/animations`); `decoration.*`
and `window.*` keep their existing owners per the RFC-0001 naming rule (no
parallel `appearance.*` block for values that already have an owner;
`appearance.theme` stays the exception). All new keys are additive; defaults
reproduce current rendering byte-identically.

## 1. Style schema: exact new keys, types, bounds, defaults, closed-vs-open

New closed table `appearance.style` (global scope). Closed means: unknown
fields reject the whole reload with a source-attributed diagnostic (existing
`undeclared` + `MAX_CONFIG_NESTED_KEYS` discipline in `bitty-lua/config.rs`);
no open catch-all, no stringly-typed escape hatch.

| Key | Type | Bounds | Default | Per-view (`views.*`)? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `appearance.style.glow_color` | `#RRGGBB` / `#RRGGBBAA` string (canonical, `<=9` bytes, existing `MAX_DECORATION_COLOR_LEN`) | parsed to `OutlineColor`; malformed rejects | unset (`None` = no glow contribution) | YES (same tier machinery as outline colors) |
| `appearance.style.glow_width` | integer logical px | `0..=16` (mirrors `MAX_DECORATION_BORDER_WIDTH_PX`) | `0` (off) | YES |
| `appearance.style.shadow_color` | `#RRGGBB` / `#RRGGBBAA` string | as above | unset (`None` = no shadow) | NO (global-only; rationale below) |
| `appearance.style.shadow_offset_x` / `shadow_offset_y` | integer logical px | `-8..=8` (new bound `MAX_STYLE_SHADOW_OFFSET_PX = 8`; keeps shadows inside the `6px` gap rhythm, never reaches content) | `0` | NO (global-only) |
| `appearance.style.shadow_blur` | RESERVED (rejected fail-closed) | — | — | — |
| `decoration.background_tint` | `#RRGGBB` / `#RRGGBBAA` string (lives in `decoration`, not `appearance.style`, per naming rule: background images are owned by the OQ-042 contract) | as above | unset (`None` = no tint) | YES (same path as `background_image`, already per-view) |
| `decoration.background_tint_strength` | float | finite within `[0.0, 1.0]` | `0.0` (no tint) | YES |
| `appearance.style.fade_unfocused` | float (global inactive-View dim factor) | finite within `[0.0, 1.0]` | `1.0` (no fade) | NO (global-only; per-view fade stays reserved under OQ-038) |
| `appearance.style.ring_alpha` | NOT ADDED (rejected from schema) | — | — | — |

Deliberate non-additions (justify-against-feasibility):
- Ring: fully covered today. Geometry + color + width = `decoration.border*`
  + `border_color*` + `border_width*` (+ per-view overrides), consumed by
  `present.rs::push_leaf_ring` as `RoundedFill{border>0}` through the SDF
  pipeline with `scale_alpha` (open/workspace/move/resize/drag fades) and
  `lerp_rgba` (focus cross-fade). A static `ring_alpha` would duplicate the
  alpha channel already in `#RRGGBBAA`; a ring *style* enum (double/dashed)
  would need new SDF fragment math — out of scope, no key reserved for it.
- Glow without new primitives: an unblurred halo is consumable TODAY as one
  extra `RoundedFill{border:0}` (solid rounded rect) sized `frame + glow_width`
  painted beneath the ring — same struct, same SDF shader, no WGSL change.
  A true *blurred* glow needs renderer work (blur pass or multi-tap halo);
  the schema therefore accepts color+width now and reserves nothing textual
  for blur: blurred glow is a renderer capability upgrade, not a schema key.
- Shadow without new primitives: a hard offset shadow is consumable TODAY as
  one `FillRect` (existing primitive) painted beneath the frame at
  `(x+off_x, y+off_y)`. Blurred shadows need renderer work; `shadow_blur` is
  RESERVED (present = whole-reload rejection, mirroring `VIEW_RESERVED_FIELDS`
  practice) until a follow-up RFC defines the blur contract + budget.
- Tint: trivially consumable — same raster-time alpha-multiply as the
  `window.background_opacity` precedent (`dim_rgba_alpha`, `sanitize_window_
  background_opacity` in `bitty-render/src/window.rs`); tint color lerps with
  the existing `lerp_rgba` when the background cross-fades. No renderer work.
- Fade: consumable as a per-leaf `scale_alpha`-style factor applied to
  Core-owned chrome fills AND glyph-instance alpha at `build_leaf_primitives`
  time for unfocused views, driven by the existing focus-transition progress
  (`animation_progress(Focus)`), so motion obeys the accepted RFC-0002
  durations/easings/reduced-motion/safe gates with zero new `AnimationKind`.
  Static factor is global-only so no per-surface opacity key (OQ-038) is
  introduced: OQ-038 stays Open; per-view fade/opacity/blur remain reserved.

Bounds rationale: widths reuse `0..=16` (paint-only ring family, never moves
the content grid — the `push_leaf_ring` invariant that content clip derives
from geometry `border`, not outline width, extends to glow/shadow: style paint
MUST NOT change cell metrics, insets, or clip rects). Shadow offset `±8`
bounds overdraw DoS (giant offsets = unbounded damage rects). Floats must be
finite (`is_finite` + range, mirroring `WindowConfig::validate` for
`opacity`/`background_opacity`); NaN/Inf/±huge reject, never coerce or clamp.
Colors reuse the outline-color canonical grammar + contrast posture (no new
contrast AC for glow/shadow/tint at this stage; tint over text inherits the
readability duty of `background_opacity` — document, do not gate v1).

`views.*` field-set delta: ADD `glow_color`, `glow_width`,
`background_tint`, `background_tint_strength` to `VIEW_ACCEPTED_FIELDS`;
`opacity`/`blur`/`animations` STAY reserved (OQ-038/OQ-043 owners unchanged);
`shadow_*` and `fade_unfocused` are global-only (rejected inside `views.*`
like `background_image_roots` is today). Field value bounds = global bounds,
unchanged (RFC-0001 rule).

## 2. Precedence + overrides

RULE: styling follows the existing two-axis model, no new axis. Axis 1 =
global layer stack from `plan.rs::LayerKind` precedence
(`CoreDefaults(0) < SystemDefaults(10) < SystemPolicy(20, non-overridable) <
Distribution(30) < Profile(40, extends-chain) < User(50) <
TrustedLocal(60) < Cli(70)`), per-field scalar-replace with source
attribution (`ConfigPlan` rules). Axis 2 = per-View selector tiers from
RFC-0001 (`*` < content-type < `ws:<label>` < `view:<ViewId>`),
order-independent, per field per View, resolved AFTER global merge
(`resolve_view_outline`/`resolve_view_background` pattern → new
`resolve_view_style`). The shorthand `CLI>file>profile>defaults` holds as the
user-visible projection of axis 1. `panel_rules` is NOT an appearance axis
(spawn/placement rules only; appearance stays out of `panel_rules` to avoid a
third resolution axis and its conflict diagnostics). `SystemPolicy` can pin
style floors/ceilings (e.g. force `fade_unfocused=1.0`) exactly like other
non-overridable entries.

Rationale (complexity vs power, fail-closed): the two-axis model is proven
(CTX-0340/0343/0347 paths), tested, and diagnosed; a third axis (per-rule or
per-plugin style) would multiply the resolution matrix, break byte-comparable
merge, and smuggle plugin-owned chrome past the Core-owns-the-frame rule
(OQ-044 stays Open — plugins supply target ids to fx verbs, never style
values). Per-view power is granted ONLY where the resolution path already
exists (glow extends the outline path; tint extends the background path);
shadow (geometry-adjacent paint, neighbor-overlap risk) and fade (uniform
inactive treatment, contrast-risk) stay global until a follow-up RFC with
renderer evidence promotes them. Every violation rejects the whole reload;
reserved-in-`views.*` rejects like `background_image_roots` does today.

## 3. Validation: fail-closed rules, reload class, safe mode

Per-key fail-closed rules (all in `bitty-config`, never in the extractor
beyond closed-set + scalar-type naming, per the `ConfigData` raw-string/leaf
split):
- `glow_width`: integer, `0..=16`, out-of-range rejects naming
  `appearance.style.glow_width` (mirror `ViewAppearanceOverride::validate`).
- `shadow_offset_x/y`: integer, `-8..=8`, rejects naming the leaf.
- Colors (`glow_color`, `shadow_color`, `background_tint`): canonical
  `#RRGGBB`/`#RRGGBBAA` parse; empty/NUL/overlong/malformed rejects (mirror
  outline-color + `validate_background_image_path` posture). No tint-contrast
  gate in v1 (documented readability duty).
- Floats (`background_tint_strength`, `fade_unfocused`): `is_finite` AND
  `[0.0, 1.0]`; NaN/Inf/out-of-range rejects (mirror `window.opacity`,
  `window.background_opacity`). Never sanitize-then-accept at the config
  layer (renderer-side `sanitize_*` stays a defense-in-depth clamp only).
- Enums: none new in v1 (no style enum) — by design, keeping the closed set
  minimal; any future enum uses `parse()->Option` + fail-closed diagnostic
  (the `AnimationEasing::parse` / `ReducedMotion::parse` pattern).
- Cross-field: `shadow_color` set with both offsets `0` paints under the
  frame (harmless, allowed — no error); `background_tint` without
  `background_image` is inert but VALID (mirrors unset-image fast path; never
  an error, never a warning-gated reject). `glow_width>0` with unset
  `glow_color` = no glow (width without color contributes nothing; valid).
- Whole-reload rejection: any single violation rejects the entire reload
  (existing `EffectiveConfig::validate` composition); `views.*`-scoped
  violations name `views[<selector>].<field>`; `ws:`/`view:` tiers resolved
  only against live state get the `validate_view_target_at` first-match
  treatment at View creation/bind/move (CTX-0343 pattern extended to the new
  per-view fields, including their AC posture).

Reload behavior: ALL new keys are `ReloadClass::Live` (append to
`LIVE_FIELDS` + table prose). Justification: every one is paint-only —
no PTY recreation, no layout re-solve, no grid-metric change; adopters
re-resolve + `pending_full_redraw` (the `set_outline_widths`/
`set_animations` precedent). No `RestartRequired` key in this schema.
Unknown/undeclared keys stay `Rejected`.

Safe mode (`bitty --safe`): extend `DecorationConfig::safe()` +
`EffectiveConfig::with_safe_decoration` to clear the new surface —
`glow_width=0`, `glow_color=None`, `shadow_*` cleared/offsets `0`,
`tint=None`/`strength=0.0`, `fade_unfocused=1.0` — AND drop/ignore `views.*`
style overrides (existing `views.clear()` covers it) AND force animation
durations `0` (existing). Rationale: safe mode promises
`0/0/1/0/0` + opaque built-in pair + instant final-state; any surviving glow,
shadow, tint, or fade would violate that promise and could mask contrast
cues. Animations already zero in safe mode, so styled fades collapse to
end-state automatically.

## 4. Application path: config → Runtime → present, live-adopt, fx consumption

Data flow (each stage existing, extended — no new stage):
1. `bitty-lua/config.rs`: extractor allow-lists grow — `appearance.style.*`
   leaves into `ConfigData` (raw strings/ints/floats, `Option` semantics:
   absent = inherit), `VIEW_ACCEPTED_FIELDS` gains the four per-view fields;
   `views.*` still rejects `shadow_*`, `fade_unfocused`, `opacity`, `blur`,
   `animations` with the offending key path named.
2. `bitty-config` (`plan` → typed validation → `merge` → `EffectiveConfig`):
   new `StyleConfig` struct (typed glow/shadow/tint/fade) with `validate()`,
   `Default` (= current rendering), `safe()`, per-field `apply_overrides`
   scalar-replace + attribution; merge-class table + `LIVE_FIELDS` + diff
   paths gain the new leaves; `resolve_view_style(&RuntimeViewTarget)` (plus
   `_traced` source variant) implements axis-2 resolution reusing the
   selector/tier/win-order code owned by the outline/background resolvers.
3. `bitty-runtime/config.rs`: `RuntimeConfig` carries resolved style next to
   `animations`/outline/background; new `RuntimeViewStyle{glow_color,
   glow_width, tint, tint_strength, fade_factor}` value type resolved per leaf
   via `view_style_for(view_id)` beside `view_outline_for`/
   `view_background_for` (same public layout state: stable `ViewId`, active
   workspace label, content kind).
4. `present.rs`: `push_leaf_ring` gains siblings `push_leaf_glow`
   (`RoundedFill{border:0}`, frame inflated by `glow_width`, color
   `scale_alpha(glow_color, open*workspace*motion)` — identical factor chain)
   and `push_leaf_shadow` (`FillRect` at offset, color likewise faded);
   background blit path multiplies tint (`dim_rgba_alpha`-family) at strength;
   `build_leaf_primitives` applies `fade_unfocused` to unfocused leaves
   through the focus-transition progress so fades animate under RFC-0002
   gates. Invariants carried over: style paints AFTER fills BEFORE glyphs
   (ring order), never alters `frame_clip`/insets/metrics; co-active
   move/resize/drag factors multiply (existing loop extended, not forked).
5. Live-adopt hooks (all in `runtime/live_config.rs` family): new
   `set_chrome_style(ResolvedStyle)` beside `set_outline_widths` /
   `set_window_opacity` / `set_theme_palette` / `set_animations`; each setter
   diffs, assigns, and sets `pending_full_redraw`; in-flight animations keep
   timing, adopt policy for subsequent triggers (the `set_animations`
   precedent). Every `LIVE_FIELDS` leaf must name its adopter (existing
   live-adopter audit extends to the new leaves).
6. fx follow-up verbs consume style (DEC-0110 consequences list names glow /
   shadow / gradient / backdrop verbs as follow-ups): verbs read the RESOLVED
   style values (`glow_color/width`, shadow params, tint) + the
   `AnimationPolicy` (closed easing incl. `spring→ease_in_out` resolution,
   durations, `enabled`/`reduced_motion`/safe gates) + the shared
   animation-budget cap; verbs supply TARGET ID ONLY (view id / window /
   band), never timing, geometry, colors, or curves — the DEC-0110
   Core-owned-chrome rule holds by construction. `pulse` stays fixed
   150ms/EaseInOut with no config change; each follow-up verb either reuses
   an accepted transition kind or proposes its `AnimationKind` + config
   grammar delta in its own RFC; no verb invents an easing outside the closed
   enum; reload needs no new keys beyond this schema; safe mode collapses
   every fx verb to no-op (existing gate).

## 5. bitty-style split line (future extension repo)

STAYS CORE (never moves): typed schema + bounds + defaults (`StyleConfig`,
`ViewAppearanceOverride` subset), fail-closed validation, layer merge +
attribution, selector grammar + tier resolution, safe-mode clearing, reload
classification + live-adopt setters, renderer consumption (`RoundedFill` /
`FillRect` / dim / fade factors), animation policy + budget, Lua
code-as-config authoring surface (`appearance.style`, `decoration.*`,
`views.*`). Rationale: these are the safety + rendering contracts; moving
them would fork validation and admit unvalidated paint.

MOVES TO `bitty-style` extension repo IF EVER CREATED (grammar + cascade
ONLY): a text stylesheet grammar (selectors, property spellings, `@`-rules —
none designed here), cascade/specificity engine COMPILED DOWN to the existing
typed `ConfigPlan` leaves (the extension is a pure frontend: text → same
bounded leaves → same fail-closed validation; it can express nothing the Lua
tables cannot), plus editor tooling (highlighting, LSP, preview). Hard
constraint: the extension MUST NOT bypass typed bounds, MUST NOT widen
`views.*` or roots policy, MUST NOT add renderer primitives; any property it
wants that has no typed leaf is rejected at compile time with a
source-attributed diagnostic (same posture as `undeclared` today).

TRIGGER CONDITION (only if): a text stylesheet language is EVER wanted —
i.e. demonstrated user demand for authoring style outside Lua PLUS an accepted
follow-up RFC defining the grammar. Until both hold, Lua tables are the
single authoring surface; NO parallel parser, NO `url()`/`@import`, NO text
cascade in core. The core schema in §1 is deliberately grammar-agnostic
(flat closed leaves) so a future compiler has stable targets.

## 6. Security notes

- New surface: four colors/widths/floats (§1), all presentation-only. No new
  file path key (tint is color-only; images still gated by
  `background_image_roots` deny-by-default + regular-file + BG-1..BG-7
  budgets), no new process/network/IPC authority, no grid/cursor/mode/
  scrollback mutation path (style reads layout ids, writes pixels only).
- Bounded-value rationale: every numeric leaf has a static ceiling
  (`0..=16` widths, `±8` offsets, finite `[0.0,1.0]` floats) enforced
  fail-closed at `ConfigPlan`, so hostile configs cannot cause unbounded
  overdraw, damage-rect explosion, or float-poisoned shaders; renderer-side
  `clamp`/`sanitize_*` remain second-layer defense only. String leaves reuse
  length + NUL + canonical-grammar gates. Config VM budgets (RC-1/RC-2, PB-1
  in ADR-0007 / Performance Budget RFC) already bound aggregate parse cost;
  no new ceiling invented (RFC-0001 §5 precedent).
- OQ-038/OQ-043 boundary respected: no per-surface opacity/blur key, no
  per-panel animation-override key is introduced; both OQs stay Open and
  their reserved rejections stay enforced — this design cannot be used to
  smuggle them early.
- NO-GO LINES (normative): no arbitrary shaders (glow/shadow reuse
  `RoundedFill`/`FillRect` + existing SDF shader; any new fragment math needs
  its own RFC + security review); no `url()` fetches / remote images (local
  approved-roots only, `--safe` opens no file); no `@import` / include
  directives (single-evaluation Lua config, existing trust + `extends`
  discipline); no expression language in style values (plain scalars only;
  Lua code-as-config executes solely under the existing Config VM sandbox +
  budgets); no plugin-writable style at runtime (Core-owned chrome; plugins
  pass target ids to gated fx verbs per DEC-0110).

## 7. Implementation task breakdown (ordered slices, acceptance sketches)

S0 — Schema + validation (bitty-config only). Add `StyleConfig` + consts
  (`MAX_STYLE_GLOW_WIDTH_PX=16`, `MAX_STYLE_SHADOW_OFFSET_PX=8`), `Default`
  (current rendering), `safe()`, `validate()`; extend
  `ViewAppearanceOverride` + `VIEW_ACCEPTED_FIELDS` mirror; merge-class
  entries + attribution; `LIVE_FIELDS` + `classify_field`; safe-clearing in
  `with_safe_decoration`. ACCEPT: unit tests per leaf (bounds incl.
  NaN/Inf/NUL/overlong), whole-reload rejection with named leaf path,
  `views[sel].field` diagnostics, safe-mode snapshot test (styled config →
  safe == unstyled defaults), `config check` green/red vectors.
S1 — Lua extractor (bitty-lua only). Parse `appearance.style.*` +
  `decoration.background_tint*` + new `views.*` fields as raw leaves;
  keep reserved rejections (`shadow_blur`, `opacity`, `blur`, `animations`,
  global-only-in-views) naming the key path. ACCEPT: extractor tests
  (absent-vs-present `Option` semantics, closed-set rejection, 64/32/4096
  caps intact), no `bitty-config` behavior change.
S2 — Resolution + runtime carry (bitty-config + bitty-runtime/config).
  `resolve_view_style[_traced]`, `RuntimeViewStyle`, `view_style_for`;
  first-match `validate_view_target_at` coverage for new per-view fields.
  ACCEPT: tier-order tests (order-independent, per-field inheritance),
  live-View first-match rejection test, traced-source assertions.
S3 — Present path (bitty-runtime + bitty-render as needed, NO new
  primitives). `push_leaf_glow`/`push_leaf_shadow`, tint multiply, focus
  fade factor with existing factor chain; live-adopt `set_chrome_style` +
  adopter audit. ACCEPT: headless pixel/golden tests (defaults byte-identical
  to pre-S3; glow/shadow/tint/fade vectors), factor-chain test (open ×
  workspace × motion), content-metrics-invariant test (clips/insets unchanged
  under max style values), reduced-motion/safe collapse tests.
S4 — fx consumption follow-ups (one verb per task, DEC-0110 pattern each:
  gated grant, intent queue, budget cap, drain-time revalidation, no new
  `AnimationKind` without RFC). ACCEPT per verb: grant-deny matrix,
  queue-cap newest-drop counting, budget bidirectionality, safe/reduced
  no-op, queued-not-applied return semantics.
S5 — bitty-style extension (ONLY on trigger §5; separate repo). Grammar +
  cascade compiler → typed leaves + tooling. ACCEPT: round-trip property
  tests (text ≡ Lua tables), compile-time rejection of unmapped properties,
  no-core-change proof (core diff empty).

Cross-cutting per slice: docs sync (config reference + reload table +
safe-mode precedence), `bitty config check` vectors, contrast-advisory
report where applicable, threat-model note (T-01 bounds / T-02-T-03 image
trust untouched). Migration/compat: purely additive; existing configs render
identically; reserved set only narrows for the four promoted per-view fields.
rationale: Lua-first code-as-config is the only authoring surface (closed typed leaves, per-field scalar-replace, source attribution); taffy is excluded because style is constrained paint-only post-cell-commit and must never move metrics, clips, or insets — admitting a flex solver would fork layout authority and break the cell-grid contract. New keys are the minimal set whose consumption needs no new renderer primitives (unblurred glow via RoundedFill, hard shadow via FillRect, tint via existing dim-multiply, fade via existing focus progress); blurred glow/shadow stay renderer work with schema leaves reserved, not half-accepted. Precedence reuses the two proven axes instead of inventing per-rule/per-plugin resolution. Safe mode clears the whole new surface. bitty-style is fenced to a future text-frontend compiling to the same leaves, created only on demonstrated demand + RFC.
title: CTX-1142 styling-system design: Lua-first appearance-tree styling schema + bitty-style split (no taffy, paint-only, closed sets, fail-closed)

context: Owner direction replaces CTX-1077 keep-slot-for-restore: floating a panel must detach it from tiling like Alt+D delete so the vacated slot collapses and siblings refill, and untoggle reinserts as a fresh split via the min-area/aspect placement policy. decision_body: Detach primitive is a new bitty-ui FloatStore mirroring the PinnedStore and ScratchpadSlot detach discipline via LayoutNode remove_leaf plus the CW-08 gate stamp, preserving ViewId. Detached floats live in a separate workspace-local store, not unified with PinnedStore: pinned is window-global sticky while floats belong to their workspace slot and stash plus load on switch. Untoggle reinserts via balanced_bisect_choice over live allocations with balanced_split_axis, ratio 0.5, after true, stamped back to Tiled with focus onto the restored leaf. Session carries per-workspace floats in memory with pin-like validation while the v3 file codec stays untouched and rejects non-empty floats fail-closed with a v4 follow-up. Focus re-home reuses the pin and scratchpad fixups with no primary hand-back on restore. Alt-drag re-anchor offsets live in a float_offsets map mirroring pinned_offsets and reset on restore while fixed-size flags ride the stored view. Zoom restores before mutation with the pin single-leaf-backup guard so a refused detach stays byte-identical.
rationale: Physical detach makes ghost chrome structurally impossible since no slot remains, and reuses the proven pin and scratchpad collapse plus focus discipline. A separate workspace-local store keeps floats from leaking across switches which unification would cause. Fresh balanced placement honors the owner placement policy instead of anchor bookkeeping. In-memory session plus fail-closed file guard avoids a half-baked codec bump. Unpin stays unchanged to honor its tested contract.

decision_body:
# Corrections to DEC-0111 (each replaces the corresponding DEC-0111 passage; everything else in DEC-0111 stands)

## Fix 1 — Shadow primitive: RoundedFill{border:0} at offset, not FillRect

DEC-0111 section 1 ("Shadow without new primitives ... as one FillRect") and
section 4 ("push_leaf_shadow (FillRect at offset ...)") are CORRECTED to:
the drop shadow is one `RoundedFill { border: 0 }` (solid rounded rect, the
same struct as the glow halo) placed at `(frame.x + shadow_offset_x,
frame.y + shadow_offset_y)` with the frame's outer radius, painted beneath
the glow/ring/fills in the existing `combined.rounded` order (shadow first,
then glow, then ring — back-to-front). Rationale, verified in
`bitty-render/src/grid.rs`: `FillRect` carries a bare `RectPx` with no radius
and would overhang the frame's rounded corners by up to `radius` px in the
corner boxes; `RoundedFill{border:0}` is documented as "paints the full solid
rounded rectangle" through the identical SDF fragment path (shared
`sd_rounded_box`, same `coverage_at`/clamping semantics as the ring), so the
shadow inherits corner-correct AA for free. The zero-new-primitives thesis
SURVIVES unchanged: shadow and glow are the same primitive with different
rect/color inputs; no WGSL, shader, or `bitty-render` type change is needed.
Bounds (`+-8` offsets, color grammar) and global-only scope are unchanged;
the offset bound additionally guarantees the inflated rounded rect stays
within the damage/gap budget. S3 acceptance gains one vector: rounded-corner
shadow golden (shadow follows frame radius, no square overhang at max radius
+ max offset).

## Fix 2 — Fade vs CTX-0386 retained leaves: invalidate or post-pass multiply

DEC-0111 section 4 ("build_leaf_primitives applies fade_unfocused to
unfocused leaves") is CORRECTED: applying the fade factor only at fresh-leaf
build time is insufficient. Verified in `present.rs`: `PresentedLeaf`
retains per-leaf `fills` + `glyphs`, and `build_leaf_primitives` reuses a
retained leaf VERBATIM when only `origin` + `scroll_offset` match (a focus
change advances neither, so clean leaves would keep stale unfaded/faded
alpha); only the ring (`push_leaf_ring`, shared by both paths) and
background blits (`CombinedLeaves::backgrounds`, rebuilt every frame) are
re-emitted per frame. This is the same reason the cursor rides a deferred
overlay instead of the retained list. S3 MUST therefore specify one of (in
order of preference): (a) retained invalidation on fade-factor change —
when the resolved fade set changes (focus move, `fade_unfocused` live-adopt,
workspace switch), drop `presented_leaf_frames` entries for affected leaves
so they re-render with the live factor (bounded: at most the visible leaf
set, same cost class as the atlas-reset rebuild); or (b) post-pass alpha
multiply — after the combined list is assembled, scale alpha of the
`fills`/`glyphs` ranges belonging to faded leaves (ranges must be tracked
per leaf during assembly since the combined list is shared). Either way the
focus-transition ANIMATION of the fade still reads the existing
`animation_progress(Focus)` value — the factor source is unchanged, only its
application point covers the reuse path. S3 invariant test is EXTENDED to
cover the retained path explicitly: (i) steady-state frame with a clean
unfocused leaf reuses retained primitives AND carries the faded alpha;
(ii) focus flip with no grid damage still repaints affected leaves with the
new factor (no stale-alpha frame observable headless); (iii) content
metrics/clips/insets still unchanged under max style values. The paint-order
and never-touch-terminal-truth invariants are unchanged.

## Fix 3 — Live-adopter audit scoped to S3 (CTX-0241 S0 precedent)

DEC-0111 section 3 ("ALL new keys are ReloadClass::Live (append to
LIVE_FIELDS)") + section 7 (S0 registers LIVE_FIELDS, S3 adds the adopter)
are CORRECTED to: S0 defines schema + validation + merge + `Default`/`safe`
and classifies the new leaves Live in the reload table, BUT the new leaves
are accepted-but-inert until S3 — parsed, validated, merged, attributed, and
reported (visible in `config show`/diff) with NO render effect — following
the `window.radius_px` CTX-0241 S0 precedent ("parsed no-op ... with no
render effect in S0"). The live-adopter audit requirement (every Live leaf
names its `set_chrome_style` adoption) is SCOPED TO S3, where the setter and
the consumption land together; S3 acceptance includes the audit proof plus a
no-stale-accept test (pre-S3 styled config validates clean AND renders
byte-identical to unstyled). No interim RestartRequired marking is needed
because inert keys require neither restart nor adoption — they are
provably unreached, which the S0 snapshot test pins. S0-S4 ordering,
bounds, defaults, and all other DEC-0111 content are otherwise APPROVED
unchanged.
rationale: Each correction was verified against the tree before recording: (1) FillRect has no radius field while RoundedFill{border:0} is the documented solid-rounded-rect SDF path — the reviewer's primitive swap keeps the zero-new-primitives claim intact and actually strengthens it (one struct for glow+shadow+ring). (2) PresentedLeaf/build_leaf_primitives verbatim-reuse vs per-frame ring/background re-emission is exactly as the reviewer described — a build-time-only fade would have shipped stale-alpha frames on every focus change without grid damage, the highest-traffic fade trigger. (3) The CTX-0241 radius_px S0 parsed-no-effect precedent resolves the audit-scope question without an interim reload-class carve-out.
title: CTX-1142 styling design corrections (PX-5855 NEEDS-FIX): shadow primitive, fade vs retained leaves, live-adopter audit scope

rationale: Defer, not go or permanent no-go. Chrome today is text plus theme-token only with fail-closed bounds, so SNI pixels would be the first third-party image ingress. Graphics caps exist but the seam migration in bitty 2000 is still open and SVG has no policy. No D-Bus presence exists today, so SNI adds a new session-bus surface needing ADR-0004 review, session-only scoping, enumeration caps, and P0-AC-005 theme reads. Menu actions must map to consented owner-verbs like ClickCommand, never raw D-Bus passthrough. L4 standing ingress, ADR-0003 DAG, registry out-of-scope row, and unverified P0 blockers all favor defer. Full rationale in issue 2014 comment.
title: SNI tray verdict: defer post-1.0 with conditions

consequences: Enforced in bitty-platform backlight_state with negative tests for both denial paths (missing grant, unpermitted backend); neither path touches the brightness file. Host task wires the live permitted probe; no Lua surface in this slice.
context: bitty#2020 requires the backlight-set privilege handling to be decided in the interface task, not discovered later. Backlight set is privileged on most systems via udev video group or polkit.
decision_body: BacklightControl.set_step attempts the brightness write only when the backend reports permitted. Otherwise it returns E_NOT_PERMITTED with a naming diagnostic. context: Users need one consistent, expressive configuration language under the per-plugin configuration root, while plugin configuration must not become an ambient code-execution or capability-granting path.
decision_body: Support a bounded Lua configuration file for each plugin. The file executes in a dedicated configuration VM with no bitty host table, plugin APIs, filesystem, network, require, or capability-granting surface and must return a plain configuration table. Enforce byte, instruction, depth, key, value, and aggregate bounds; accept only manifest-declared keys; fail closed to shipped defaults on errors. New Lua configuration wins over old TOML.
rationale: Lua is already the project configuration language and has a sandboxed execution model, while TOML remains useful as a migration fallback. Directory-scoped configuration supports user customization without plugin-id filename collisions. Explicitly separating the configuration VM from the plugin VM preserves the no-ambient-authority boundary.
